evidence: Blog (Yue Jia, Ke Mao, Mark Harman, Sep 13 2018): "it is not designed to deploy fixes to production code on its own." "When its patches are fully tested, SapFix sends them to a human reviewer for approval."
correction: Authors: Yue Jia, Ke Mao, Mark Harman (Meta Engineering blog).

evidence: Abstract: fixes bugs "reported by popular static analyzers for Java"; "we report on deploying the approach within Facebook"; "Getafix is the first industrially-deployed automated bug-fixing tool that learns fix patterns from past, human-written fixes".
correction: Bader, Scott, Pradel, Chandra; arXiv 2019, published OOPSLA 2019 (PACMPL) [verify venue]. Quote is a truncation of a longer sentence that continues '...that learns fix patterns from past, human-written fixes'.

evidence: Abstract: "Repairnator is a bot. It constantly monitors software bugs discovered during continuous integration of open-source software"; "5 patches that were accepted by the human developers and permanently merged".
correction: Monperrus, Urli, Durieux, Martinez, Baudry, Seinturier; arXiv Oct 2018. Note patches were proposed under a fake human identity.

evidence: Abstract: "it has studied 11 317 test failures over 1 609 open-source software projects hosted on GitHub, and has generated patches for 17 different bugs."
correction: Urli, Yu, Seinturier, Monperrus; ICSE-SEIP 2018 (DOI 10.1145/3183519.3183540); arXiv posted Nov 2018.

evidence: Abstract: "The overwhelming majority of the reported patches are not correct and are equivalent to a single modification that simply deletes functionality." Scope: GenProg, RSRepair, AE.
correction: Scope claim to reported patches of GenProg, RSRepair and AE (not all G&V systems). Qi, Long, Achour, Rinard, ISSTA 2015.

evidence: Sec. 1: "one test suite is training data used to construct a patch, and the other is evaluation or held-out data used to evaluate the quality of the patch."
correction: Smith, Barr, Le Goues, Brun, ESEC/FSE 2015. Claim is a methodological recommendation inferred from their design; quote is in Sec. 1, not the abstract.

evidence: Abstract: "Our approach successfully prevented 56.3% of the incorrect patches to be generated, without blocking any correct patches." Evaluated on 139 patches.
correction: Xiong, Liu, Zeng, Zhang, Huang; ICSE 2018 (arXiv v1 2017). Dataset is only 139 patches.

evidence: Abstract: "observes normal executions to learn invariants..."; Red Team "developed ten code-injection exploits"; "ClearView detected and blocked all of the attacks. For seven of the ten exploits, ClearView automatically generated patches".
correction: Perkins et al., SOSP 2009. Note ClearView patches binaries without human intervention (contrast with fiks's human-merge gate).
